title: Applied GIS research behind specialised applications

blocks.text: GIS application research examined problems hidden from the end user. Daniel Gerard O’Donohue’s 2010 Canterbury MSc investigated automatic correction of spatial misalignment between directly georeferenced aerial thermal imagery and building-footprint vector data. Its feature-matching approach was designed to improve positional accuracy when mapped datasets were combined. This was a defined research contribution to integrating imagery and vector information, rather than an inventory of every subsequent operational application.

blocks.text: Hussam Al-Mahoozi’s 2011 Otago Master of Business examined the use of Dunedin City Council’s GIS for city retail planning. The institutional thesis record establishes the business and local-government planning context, but does not establish any specific later system changes adopted by the council. Together, these research projects show that a useful map application depends on underlying data quality as well as on how the application supports a planning decision.
